title: Kernel Health Index and Oncall Investigation Playbook
author: Priya Radhakrishnan
body:
Summary:
This page defines the Kernel Health Index (KHI) — a composite signal used to detect regressions and degradation in the serving runtime’s kernel layer — and provides a step-by-step oncall investigation and remediation playbook. The KHI aggregates kernel-level telemetry (latency, error rates, kernel queue lengths, preemption events, and GPU memory pressure) into a single, interpretable score per scheduler cohort. The goal is early, actionable detection with minimal false positives and clear escalation steps.

Why we need KHI:
- Kernels are a frequent choke point for tail latency and cross-tenant interference.
- Single-signal alerts (e.g., p50 token latency) are noisy when mixed workloads or rolling deploys are active.
- KHI provides a stable, cohort-scoped index that surfaces meaningful kernel-level change while preserving correlation to user-visible SLOs.

Scope and ownership:
- Scope: GPU kernel operations and the scheduler/handoff surface inside the runtime (kernel invocation, queueing, preemption, kernel handoff errors, kernel timeouts).
- Owning team: eng-serving-runtime (runtime kernel and scheduling subteams).
- Oncall escalation: runtime oncall -> kernel scheduling rotate -> runtime performance owners.

KHI definition (high level):
- KHI is a normalized, weighted sum of standardized component signals for a cohort and 1-minute window:
  - Latency sensitive kernel tail (K_tail): percentile-based tail of kernel execution time (e.g., 99th percentile of measured kernel time).
  - Kernel error spike score (K_err): count of kernel-level errors (failed launches, launch timeouts) normalized by request volume.
  - Queue pressure index (K_q): average queue length / slot capacity ratio in scheduler queues.
  - Preemption churn (K_preempt): count of preemption events per minute normalized by active kernels.
  - Memory pressure index (K_mem): fraction of kernels that triggered OOM/soft-OOM or elevated allocation/reclaim events.

- Simplified score formula (illustrative):
  KHI = 100 * (0.35*norm(K_tail) + 0.25*norm(K_err) + 0.15*norm(K_q) + 0.15*norm(K_preempt) + 0.10*norm(K_mem))
  where norm(x) maps the raw metric to [0,1] using cohort-specific baseline percentiles (historical 7d median + MAD).

Interpretation buckets:
- KHI < 15: healthy. No action required.
- 15 <= KHI < 40: watch. Add to daily telemetry digest and correlate with SLO deltas.
- 40 <= KHI < 70: alert to oncall. Start triage checklist.
- KHI >= 70: high-priority incident. Execute mitigation matrix and page kernel scheduling owners.

PromQL and query recipes (examples):
- 99th percentile kernel exec time per cohort (example):
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(kernel_exec_duration_seconds_bucket{cohort="web-embeddings"}[5m])) by (le, cohort))

- Kernel error spike (5m):
  sum(rate(kernel_launch_errors_total{cohort="web-embeddings"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kernel_invocations_total{cohort="web-embeddings"}[5m]))

- Queue pressure (1m avg):
  avg_over_time(scheduler_queue_length{queue=~"kernel-.*",cohort="web-embeddings"}[1m]) / scheduler_queue_capacity{cohort="web-embeddings"}

- Preemption churn (1m):
  sum(rate(kernel_preemptions_total{cohort="web-embeddings"}[1m])) / max(1, sum(rate(kernel_invocations_total{cohort="web-embeddings"}[1m])))

- Memory pressure (ratio):
  sum(rate(kernel_memory_pressure_events_total{cohort="web-embeddings"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kernel_invocations_total{cohort="web-embeddings"}[5m]))

Alerting rules (recommended thresholds):
- KHI Alert (page): KHI >= 40 for 2m sustained OR KHI delta >= 25 in 5m. Severity: P2 (first responder), escalate to P1 if sustained > 10m or correlated SLO breach.
- Kernel error rate guide: kernel_launch_error_rate > 0.005 (0.5%) sustained 5m -> generate paging alert.
- Queue pressure guide: scheduler_queue_length / capacity > 0.7 for 3m -> fire warning; >0.9 -> page.

Oncall investigation checklist (ordered):
1) Confirm alert and scope
   - Look at KHI time series and cohort tag. Is the spike localized to one cohort or global?
   - Check related SLO dashboards (token latency, request success rate) for correlation.
2) Immediately gather fast artifacts (first 2 minutes)
   - grep or use trace UI to collect 5–20 traces that hit altered kernels.
   - Snapshot kernel metrics: kernel_exec_duration_seconds, kernel_launch_errors_total, scheduler_queue_length, kernel_preemptions_total, kernel_memory_pressure_events_total.
   - Capture top-10 affected hosts/pods and GPU IDs.
3) Triage for common fault classes (parallelizable):
   - Regression in kernel binary/driver: check recent kernel-related rollouts or kernel-variant canaries in the last 30m. Command: git rev-list --since="30 minutes ago" -- kernel/
   - Resource exhaustion: look at node GPU memory util and host-level OOM logs. CLI examples: kubectl top pod -n runtime | sort -k3 -nr; ssh to host and check nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv
   - Scheduler misconfiguration: check admission-controller and credit buckets for cohort. Query admission metrics and recent config pushes.
   - Hot-path kernel slowdown due to sequence length change: correlate request sequence_length histogram to kernel latency.
4) Apply fast mitigations (choose applicable, run one at a time):
   - Route affected cohort to safe model variant or lower fidelity model to reduce kernel load. (Console route change; follow routing rollback checklist.)
   - Increase scheduler slots or temporarily widen admission (if SLO permits).
   - Abort rollout: revert recent kernel or kernel-config change via canary rollback.
   - Evict noisy tenant(s) if cross-tenant noise is identified (follow eviction authority policy).
5) If mitigations fail, page kernel scheduling owner and SRE with incident severity.

Post-incident diagnostics and writeup (10 steps):
1) Capture full 1h/24h metric windows and annotate the KHI spike and mitigations applied.
2) Replay sample traces with throttling reproduction harness (use the replay-runbook below).
3) Run targeted microbenchmarks against suspected kernels (see section: microbenchmark recipes).
4) Check for correlated infra events (network blips, cloud NPU maintenance notices, host reboots).
5) Extract kernel flame graphs and differential profiles against a pre-incident baseline.
6) If a new kernel variant is implicated, run the compatibility test matrix and kernel-safety smoke tests.
7) Update KHI normalizers if the baseline has shifted legitimately due to new model mix.
8) Produce a short incident summary with root cause, corrective actions, and preventive work.
9) Link a follow-up ticket with owners and target dates for any code/config change.
10) Verify remediation by validating KHI and SLOs for 48–72 hours.

Microbenchmark recipes (quick):
- Controlled invocation: run the kernel microbench driver with varying sequence lengths and batch shapes to reproduce tail behavior. Example command: 
  ./kernel_microbench --model=decoder_v2 --batch-shape=1x64x512 --sequence=1024 --repeat=200

- Kernel launch stress: synthetic parallel launch script to exercise launch paths. 
  python tools/parallel_launch.py --workers=128 --ops=2000 --cohort=web-embeddings

Observability changes to implement (backlog):
- Add KHI cohort breakdown to the daily perf digest email and Console uptime dashboard.
- Store 7d sliding baseline histograms per cohort to make normalization robust to diurnal patterns.
- Introduce automatic root-cause candidate ranking: link top correlated signals and host/pod lists in alert payload.

Known limitations and caveats:
- KHI can be biased during large deployments or A/B experiments; always annotate major rollouts and use rollouts tag to mute alerts during coordination windows.
- The normalization function requires 7d stable baseline; newly onboarded cohorts with <24h data should use default baseline.
- Cross-tier routing events can create transient KHI spikes; correlate routing events to avoid unnecessary paging.

Example incident timeline (short):
- 09:02 KHI crosses 40 for cohort web-embeddings.
- 09:03 Oncall investigation started; top 5 hosts show GPU memory pressure.
- 09:05 Route impacted cohort to quantized variant; KHI falls to 22 within 6 minutes.
- 09:30 Root cause identified: canary kernel variant introduced a memory growth regression.
- Postmortem: canary gate tightened; new safety test added to microbenchmark suite.

Appendix A — Sample alert payload (suggested fields):
- alert_name: kernel_health_index_high
- cohort: web-embeddings
- khi_value: 73
- khi_delta_5m: 38
- top_metrics: {k_tail: 0.99, k_err: 0.007, k_q: 0.85, k_preempt: 0.12, k_mem: 0.22}
- top_hosts: [ip-10-1-12-3, ip-10-1-13-9]
- recent_rollouts: [kernel-variant-1.7.2, scheduler-config-2026-11-12]

Appendix B — Example canary mute policy (operational):
- During a scheduled kernel canary (window: 30m), KHI alerts are muted if canary_rollout_tag=true AND KHI increase is restricted to canary cohort only. Non-canary cohort impact always pages.

Appendix C — Links and references:
- Runtime telemetry data model: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/team-wiki/runtime-telemetry-sampling-cost-aware-profiling-2027
- Scheduler admission matrix: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/kernel-admission-matrix-and-signal-negotiation-manual-2026
- Microbenchmark suite: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/microbenchmark-suite-variance-analysis-2025

If you are oncall and unsure, follow the checklist under 'Confirm alert and scope' and escalate immediately. This playbook will be iterated on after each incident and quarterly review by the kernel scheduling team.
